validated_results.title: Identification of an Epoxide Metabolite of Lycopene in Human Plasma Using <sup>13</sup>C-Labeling and QTOF-MS.
validated_results.reason: This is a plasma metabolite identification study using 13C-labeling and LC-QTOF-MS to characterize lycopene oxidative metabolism, providing no evidence on tomato intake and prostate cancer incidence.

validated_results.title: Processed meat and selected hormone-related cancers.
validated_results.reason: Hospital-based case-control analysis reporting an odds ratio for high versus low processed meat consumption and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: highest (≥20 g/d) vs lowest (<10 g/d) category of processed meat consumption
extraction.population: hospital-based cases of hormone-related cancers and controls

cases.excerpt: These studies included 5981 cases of cancer of the breast, 992 of the endometrium, 2002 of the ovary, 1582 of the prostate, and a total of 16 394 controls with data on processed meat.

effect_size.excerpt: The OR for the highest (≥20 g/d) compared with lowest (<10 g/d) category of processed meat consumption was 1.16 (95% CI 1.06-1.28) for breast, 1.31 (95% CI 1.07-1.60) for endometrial, 1.49 (95% CI 1.30-1.71) for ovarian, and 0.89 (95% CI 0.74-1.07) for prostate cancer.

confidence_interval.excerpt: The OR for the highest (≥20 g/d) compared with lowest (<10 g/d) category of processed meat consumption was 1.16 (95% CI 1.06-1.28) for breast, 1.31 (95% CI 1.07-1.60) for endometrial, 1.49 (95% CI 1.30-1.71) for ovarian, and 0.89 (95% CI 0.74-1.07) for prostate cancer.

comparison.excerpt: the highest (≥20 g/d) compared with lowest (<10 g/d) category of processed meat consumption

design.excerpt: an integrated network of hospital-based case-control studies

timing.excerpt: conducted between 1982 and 2006 in various Italian areas

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The median consumption of processed meat in this population was 2 portions per wk

validated_results.title: Iron status in relation to cancer risk and mortality: Findings from a population-based prospective study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective case-cohort study of prediagnostic serum iron status markers with incident prostate cancer risk reported as a null association.

extraction.population: population-based cohort participants with incident cancer cases and a random subcohort

sample_size.excerpt: A case-cohort sample of the population-based EPIC-Heidelberg Study including a random subcohort (n = 2738) and incident cases of breast cancer (n = 627), prostate cancer (n = 554), lung cancer (n = 195), colorectal cancer (n = 256) and cancer death (n = 759) was used. Ferritin levels were inversely associated with breast cancer risk in the multivariable Cox regression model, with a hazard ratio (HR) of 0.67 [95% confidence interval: 0.49, 0.92] for women in the highest quartile compared to those in the lowest quartile.

cases.excerpt: A case-cohort sample of the population-based EPIC-Heidelberg Study including a random subcohort (n = 2738) and incident cases of breast cancer (n = 627), prostate cancer (n = 554), lung cancer (n = 195), colorectal cancer (n = 256) and cancer death (n = 759) was used.

design.excerpt: A case-cohort sample of the population-based EPIC-Heidelberg Study

timing.excerpt: we evaluated prediagnostic serum concentrations of ferritin, iron and transferrin

exposure_measurement.excerpt: prediagnostic serum concentrations of ferritin, iron and transferrin as well as transferrin saturation (TSAT)
